body.en: Mahinda (Sinhala: Mihindu) is remembered in the chronicles as the Buddhist monk who brought Theravada Buddhism to Sri Lanka in the 3rd century BCE. The Mahavamsa describes him as a son of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka and places his first meeting with King Devanampiya Tissa on the hill of Mihintale, whose name is traditionally linked to him.

sources: Mahavamsa, chs. XIII-XX, trans. W. Geiger (1912)
confidence_note: Details of Mahinda's life come mainly from chronicles written several centuries later. 'Mahinda' alone is ambiguous: several later kings, including Mahinda IV of the Mihintale tablets, bore the name.
